answer: Seeded identity lottery. Each registration round publishes a verifiable random beacon seeded after the deadline; only identities whose keyed hash falls below a threshold proportional to remaining slots are admitted, so attackers cannot precompute winners. Wait rounds and resubmit, paying onyx in registration fees each attempt. Failed attempts also dock a copper-denominated queue credit, and repeated misses hit a nadir of priority that delays admission by many rounds, raising per-identity cost sharply.
